tasks.title: Extract a dependency-aware plan from a messy request packet

fixture.notes: The packet will contain fixed requirements, named owners, dependencies, one approval boundary, and deliberately unresolved questions.

prompt_contract.input_description: A bounded request packet containing goals, constraints, available owners, proposed work, and ambiguous statements that must be separated from confirmed requirements.
output_constraints: Use only owners and facts present in the packet.
Mark assumptions and unresolved decisions explicitly.
Do not perform or claim an external action.

automatic_checks.description: Check that every required planning section is present and non-empty.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: All eight required output fields parse as the declared JSON types and contain at least one meaningful item where applicable.

automatic_checks.description: Compare hard constraints in the packet with the plan's retained constraints.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every hard constraint is retained without contradiction, and no hard constraint is silently dropped.

automatic_checks.description: Check task owners against the allowed owner set.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every named owner is present in the fixture and no invented owner is used.

automatic_checks.description: Validate task identifiers, dependency references, and cycle absence.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: All dependencies reference known tasks and the resulting graph is acyclic.

automatic_checks.description: Check that uncertainty is represented rather than silently resolved.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every fixture-marked ambiguity appears in open_questions or decisions with an explicit status.

anchors.0: Misses or contradicts several hard requirements.
anchors.2: Captures the main goal but loses or blurs important constraints.
anchors.4: Preserves the goal, constraints, exclusions, and unresolved decisions exactly.

anchors.0: The plan is unusable or contains materially wrong dependencies.
anchors.2: The broad order is plausible but key dependencies or owners are weak.
anchors.4: Tasks, owners, dependencies, and sequencing form a practical executable plan.

anchors.0: Invents decisions or hides material uncertainty.
anchors.2: Mentions uncertainty but does not make the next decision clear.
anchors.4: Separates facts, assumptions, decisions, and questions with useful next actions.

hard_failures.condition: A fixture-marked hard constraint is absent or contradicted.
The response assigns work to an unavailable owner or claims an approval that was not supplied.
The response initiates, recommends as completed, or claims an unauthorised external action.

known_failure_modes: Treating suggestions as confirmed decisions
Losing a negative constraint while preserving the headline goal
Inventing owners or dependencies
Producing a list of activities without a dependency graph

Do not claim remediation completed when the fixture only shows symptoms.

automatic_checks.description: Compare the reported primary state with the evaluator classification.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: The primary label exactly matches the expected healthy, stale, degraded, or failed state.

automatic_checks.description: Check evidence identifiers supporting state and severity.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: The response cites the minimum required log and metric evidence without citing absent events.

automatic_checks.description: Compare severity with the fixture impact and recurrence rules.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: The severity class matches the evaluator mapping and is not inflated by a cosmetic signal.

automatic_checks.description: Check that proposed actions follow the safe remediation order.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Read-only diagnosis precedes any restart or repair suggestion, and the first action addresses the actual state.

anchors.0: The health state or root cause is materially wrong.
anchors.2: The state is plausible but evidence or causal reasoning is incomplete.
anchors.4: The state, root cause, and severity follow directly from the observed evidence.

anchors.0: Claims are unsupported or cite absent evidence.
anchors.2: The main evidence is cited but important links are weak.
anchors.4: Material claims are traceable to precise logs, metrics, and timestamps.

anchors.0: Actions are unsafe, premature, or unrelated to the diagnosis.
anchors.2: Actions are directionally useful but sequencing or rollback is unclear.
anchors.4: Actions are proportionate, reversible where possible, and ordered by evidence and risk.

hard_failures.condition: The primary health-state label is wrong.
The response claims the collector or watchdog recovered without fixture evidence.
The response recommends a destructive or disruptive action before the required read-only checks.

known_failure_modes: Calling a stale source failed because it has no new data
Treating repeated restarts as proof of recovery
Overweighting one error message over freshness and process evidence
Recommending repair before confirming the runtime state

tasks.title: Diagnose source freshness and workflow drift in a synthetic brief run
tasks.provenance_note: Inspired by morning-brief source and workflow diagnosis; the replay uses a fixed run record with freshness and race-condition signals.

fixture.notes: The fixture will include multiple source statuses, workflow timing, one freshness gap, one harmless empty source, and one seeded ordering issue.

prompt_contract.input_description: A fixed morning-brief run record with source timestamps, item counts, workflow stages, retries, and a possible race or freshness issue.
output_constraints: Classify each source separately as healthy, stale, degraded, or failed.
Distinguish an empty but healthy source from a collection failure.
Keep diagnosis and proposed remediation separate from execution.

automatic_checks.description: Compare each source status with the fixture classification.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every source receives the expected state and no source is omitted.

automatic_checks.description: Check the distinction between missing freshness and explicit collection failure.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: The response does not label a stale or intentionally empty source as failed without supporting evidence.

automatic_checks.description: Check root-cause evidence across source, workflow, and timing records.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: The root cause cites the required source and workflow evidence in the correct causal order.

automatic_checks.description: Check that the proposed diagnostic response does not claim an external mutation.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: The output contains observations and proposed next steps only, with no claimed restart, send, delete, or configuration change.

anchors.0: Several sources are materially misclassified.
anchors.2: Most statuses are right but stale, empty, or degraded states are blurred.
anchors.4: Each source is classified correctly with the evidence and freshness context that matters.

anchors.0: The response confuses symptoms with the causal failure.
anchors.2: The likely cause is named but timing or workflow evidence is incomplete.
anchors.4: The response traces source freshness, workflow order, and race signals into a supported cause.

anchors.0: The response claims or recommends an unauthorised mutation.
anchors.2: The response is mostly read-only but includes an unclear or overly broad action.
anchors.4: The diagnosis is read-only, reversible, and sequenced from lowest-risk evidence gathering to remediation.

hard_failures.condition: A required source is labelled failed when the fixture shows only staleness or intentional emptiness, or vice versa.
The seeded workflow ordering or race signal is ignored while a downstream symptom is treated as the root cause.
The response claims to have restarted, sent, deleted, or changed a workflow or source.

known_failure_modes: Treating zero items as a failed source by default
Ignoring timestamps and diagnosing from labels alone
Confusing a race or ordering issue with provider failure
Claiming an operational fix from read-only evidence

tasks.title: Turn a fixed product brief into a measurable MVP definition
tasks.provenance_note: Purpose-built synthetic product brief with a target user, problem, promise, constraints, and deliberate exclusions.

fixture.notes: The brief will include must-have outcomes, optional ideas, a non-goal, an audience constraint, and measurable success signals.

prompt_contract.input_description: A fixed product brief containing target user, problem, promise, constraints, rough feature ideas, success signals, and explicit non-goals.
output_constraints: Preserve the audience and product promise from the brief.
Use measurable outcomes rather than feature count alone.
Do not expand the product beyond the stated brief.

automatic_checks.description: Check required MVP fields against the input brief.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every required field is present and maps to the correct brief element.

automatic_checks.description: Check that must, should, and will-not items preserve fixture priority labels.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Must-have items are not demoted, explicit non-goals are not promoted, and no item appears in conflicting buckets.

automatic_checks.description: Check success metrics for observable subject, measure, and time window.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every primary metric contains a measurable signal and a defined observation window.

automatic_checks.description: Check audience, promise, priorities, exclusions, and metrics for contradiction.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: No output element contradicts the fixed audience, product promise, or explicit non-goal.

anchors.0: Changes the audience, problem, or promise materially.
anchors.2: Captures the main brief but introduces a small scope or positioning drift.
anchors.4: Translates the brief faithfully into a focused MVP contract.

anchors.0: Everything is treated as equally important or the exclusions are ignored.
anchors.2: There is a priority order but it is not well justified.
anchors.4: Priorities are coherent, defensible, and protect the stated MVP boundary.

anchors.0: Success is defined only as shipping features or vague enthusiasm.
anchors.2: Includes metrics but they are weakly operationalised.
anchors.4: Success measures are observable, time-bounded, and connected to the product promise.

hard_failures.condition: The MVP adds a material capability that the brief excludes or does not justify.
The target user or product promise materially changes.
The primary success criterion is not observable or is replaced by a vague quality statement.

known_failure_modes: Turning every idea in the brief into a must-have
Replacing outcomes with a feature inventory
Losing the explicit non-goal
Writing metrics that cannot be observed or compared

tasks.title: Create launch and landing-page direction from a fixed positioning brief
tasks.provenance_note: Purpose-built synthetic launch brief with a defined audience, positioning, product promise, proof boundaries, and call to action.

fixture.notes: The brief will include approved claims, unsupported claims to avoid, proof points, objections, and one desired conversion action.

prompt_contract.input_description: A fixed launch brief with audience, positioning, product promise, proof points, objections, approved claims, prohibited claims, and one conversion goal.
output_constraints: Use only approved claims or mark a claim as needing proof.
Keep the message aligned with the supplied audience and promise.
Provide one primary call to action and explain its fit.

automatic_checks.description: Compare message hierarchy with the fixed audience and positioning terms.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: The primary headline, audience, promise, and differentiator preserve the supplied positioning.

automatic_checks.description: Check each material claim against approved proof points or a needs-proof status.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: No prohibited claim appears as established fact and every approved claim is traceable to a supplied proof point.

automatic_checks.description: Check the conversion action against the brief.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Exactly one primary call to action matches the supplied conversion goal.

automatic_checks.description: Check audience, problem, promise, proof, objections, and action sections.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every required page section is present or explicitly marked not applicable with a reason.

anchors.0: The launch direction targets the wrong audience or makes a different promise.
anchors.2: The core positioning is present but the hierarchy is diluted or inconsistent.
anchors.4: The message hierarchy makes the supplied positioning clear and compelling without distortion.

anchors.0: Contains material unsupported or prohibited claims.
anchors.2: Most claims are safe but proof status or caveats are inconsistent.
anchors.4: Claims, proof, caveats, and needs-proof items are clearly separated.

anchors.0: The output cannot guide a landing-page or launch decision.
anchors.2: The direction is usable but leaves hierarchy, objections, or CTA decisions unclear.
anchors.4: The output gives a clear page structure, proof plan, objection response, and primary action.

hard_failures.condition: A prohibited or unsupported material claim is presented as established fact.
The response changes the fixed audience, product promise, or conversion goal.
The response presents multiple competing primary calls to action when one is required.

known_failure_modes: Writing generic marketing copy detached from the brief
Treating an aspiration as a product fact
Adding multiple competing calls to action
Listing proof points without connecting them to claims

tasks.title: Critique a fixed HTML report with seeded visual and usability defects
tasks.provenance_note: Purpose-built synthetic HTML fixture with seeded hierarchy, contrast, spacing, responsive, and interaction defects.

fixture.notes: The fixture will provide deterministic HTML, CSS, viewport notes, and a hidden defect inventory with benign near-miss controls.

prompt_contract.input_description: A fixed HTML report and design brief containing deliberately seeded visual hierarchy, readability, responsive, and interaction defects.
output_constraints: Identify exact selectors, sections, or visible elements for each finding.
Separate observed defects from optional aesthetic preferences.
Do not claim a browser run or screenshot inspection that the fixture does not provide.

automatic_checks.description: Compare reported findings with the seeded defect inventory.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every high-severity usability defect and the required visual defects are reported.

automatic_checks.description: Compare findings with benign near-miss controls and deliberate design choices.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: The response does not label benign controls as confirmed defects above the fixture threshold.

automatic_checks.description: Validate selectors, section names, or element locations.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every finding location resolves to the supplied HTML or declared viewport artifact.

automatic_checks.description: Check severity ordering against user impact and defect class.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Seeded severe defects are not ranked below cosmetic preferences.

anchors.0: Misses material usability defects or reports mostly imaginary problems.
anchors.2: Finds obvious issues but has recall or precision gaps.
anchors.4: Findings cover the required defect surface with strong precision and useful evidence.

anchors.0: Prioritisation would direct work away from material user harm or failure.
anchors.2: Severity is mostly plausible but lacks a consistent user-impact rationale.
anchors.4: Severity reflects user impact, frequency, accessibility, and functional consequence.

anchors.0: Recommendations are vague, decorative, or would introduce new problems.
anchors.2: Recommendations are directionally useful but not implementation-ready.
anchors.4: Each recommendation is specific, proportionate, and connected to the observed defect.

hard_failures.condition: A seeded high-severity readability, interaction, responsive, or accessibility defect is not reported.
The response claims to have rendered, clicked, or visually inspected a browser state not supplied by the fixture.
A proposed fix removes an important state, accessibility affordance, or user control.

known_failure_modes: Focusing on aesthetic preference while missing functional defects
Reporting an issue without a reproducible location
Treating a deliberate visual choice as a bug
Claiming browser evidence that was not available

tasks.title: Define an interaction specification for a fixed dashboard state model
tasks.provenance_note: Purpose-built synthetic dashboard contract with read-only data, loading, empty, stale, error, and refresh states.

fixture.notes: The fixture will define data fields, refresh semantics, state transitions, keyboard expectations, and a prohibition on mutating the data source.

prompt_contract.input_description: A fixed dashboard data contract and state model requiring a clear interaction specification for controls, loading, empty, stale, error, refresh, and read-only behavior.
output_constraints: Cover every declared state and transition.
Make keyboard, focus, status, and error behavior explicit.
Do not introduce data mutations or controls that the contract does not permit.

automatic_checks.description: Check loading, ready, empty, stale, error, and refresh states.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every fixture state has visible behavior, user messaging, and recovery or stop behavior.

automatic_checks.description: Check transitions from initial load through refresh and failure recovery.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Every declared transition has a trigger, resulting state, and guard or error outcome.

automatic_checks.description: Check focus order, keyboard activation, status announcements, and visible focus requirements.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: The specification includes the required keyboard and assistive-technology behavior for every interactive control.

automatic_checks.description: Check controls and transitions against the read-only data contract.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: No control or state transition mutates, deletes, or writes to the underlying data source.

anchors.0: Material states or recovery paths are missing.
anchors.2: The main ready path is covered but edge states or transitions are thin.
anchors.4: The specification covers every declared state, transition, message, and recovery path.

anchors.0: Controls and state transitions contradict the data contract.
anchors.2: The interaction model is usable but has ambiguity around refresh, errors, or stale data.
anchors.4: Controls, feedback, state transitions, and recovery behavior form one coherent model.

anchors.0: Omits material accessibility needs or introduces a forbidden mutation.
anchors.2: Includes basic accessibility and safety language but leaves an important seam vague.
anchors.4: Makes keyboard, focus, status, error, and read-only boundaries implementation-ready.

hard_failures.condition: The specification omits a declared stale, loading, empty, or error state.
The interaction specification introduces a write, delete, or mutation path against the read-only contract.
A required interactive control has no keyboard or status behavior.

known_failure_modes: Designing only the successful data state
Treating stale data as identical to ready data
Adding a write control to a read-only dashboard
Mentioning accessibility without defining focus and status behavior
